6.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
6.text: "Thank you for being here so early on this glorious day in spite of the emergency, Mr. President and Mr. Vice President."

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: We got out of the car and walked towards the entrance of the building, escorted by our guards. Besides our own security forces, I noticed a heavy police presence.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: The buildings around the plaza were decorated with a comically large amount of Sordish flags. Everywhere I looked, I saw a sea of maroon, white and gold.

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: At the entrance, Kesaro Kibener, the head of the National Front Party, was waiting for us in his iconic brown suit, together with a group of local policemen.

13.speaker: Petr Vectern
13.text: "Huh. I thought we arrived way too early. Looks like our host -- the devil himself -- is already expecting us."

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: We got out of the car and walked towards the entrance of the building, escorted by our guards.

15.speaker: Petr Vectern
15.text: "Why is he even in the spotlight? He's acting like he still governs the city."

16.speaker: Player
16.text: "Honestly, I'm already regretting my decision to come here."

17.speaker: Player
17.text: "To be fair, his party still does."

18.speaker: Player
18.text: "He's a dangerously competent man, Petr. We should be cautious with him."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "He can act however he wants, Petr. He is not a threat to us."

24.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
24.text: "Thank you for being here so early on this glorious day, Mr. President and Mr. Vice President."

25.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
25.text: "As the former mayor of Jen, it is an honor to welcome you to our fine city."

29.speaker: Player
29.text: "It looks like you did a good job. Maybe you should think about running for local office again."

30.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
30.text: "Thanks for the kind words, but I'll do an even better job as president. Besides, as you can see, our current mayor doesn't need my help."

31.speaker: Petr Vectern
31.text: "Thank you for organizing this, Mr. Kibener."

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: Seeing us arrive, Kesaro approached us with a smile.

34.speaker: Narrator
34.text: Kesaro pointed at the center of the plaza where a stage had been erected. He gestured at the blazing sun above us.

35.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
35.text: "It'll still be a while before the stage is ready. Why don't we find somewhere away from the sun?"

37.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
37.text: "Let's brighten up a little. It's Victory Day today."

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: After passing one more cigarette to Petr, he lit them up.

41.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
41.text: "I just wanted to use this opportunity to make some comments on the administration."

42.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
42.text: "It isn't everyday that one sees the president and the vice president together, let alone have a conversation with them. Surely you'd understand."

44.speaker: Player
44.text: "Well, there's nothing better to do right now. Go ahead and make your comments if you have to."

45.speaker: Player
45.text: "I'll be very honest. I don't want to hear your comments. Please keep them to yourself."

46.speaker: Player
46.text: "Thank you, Mr. Kibener. I appreciate your supportive words."

47.speaker: Player
47.text: "I'm glad you approve. And frankly, I don't think you and I are so different from each other."

48.speaker: Player
48.text: "Thank you, Mr. Kibener, but I don't need either your sympathy or your support."

49.speaker: Player
49.text: "Are you serious? *Not enough*? It's an emergency, Mr. Kibener. What more can I do?"

50.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
50.text: "I meant no offense, Mr. President. You've done wonders to neutralize the Red Youth. But the Bludish separatists are just as dangerous as the commies, if not more."

51.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
51.text: "I meant no offense, Mr. President. You've done wonders to neutralize the separatists. But the Red Youth is as equally dangerous as the Bluds."

52.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
52.text: "If only something could be done against them as well..."

56.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
56.text: "I wouldn't dare to disagree with that."

58.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
58.text: "Let's brighten up a little. It's Victory Day today."

62.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
62.text: "Let's brighten up a little. It's Victory Day today."

64.speaker: Player
64.text: "You'll be making a grave mistake if you keep supporting terrorists like the Young Sords, Mr. Kibener."

65.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
65.text: "Just because you label them a terrorist organization doesn't make them one, Mr. Rayne."

67.speaker: Player
67.text: "It was a necessary decision. That's all I can say."

68.speaker: Player
68.text: "Mistakes were made, but the past is in the past."

69.speaker: Player
69.text: "Am I supposed to be impressed with these theatrics?"

70.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
70.text: "It was hardly a *necessary* decision, Mr. President. You know that."

71.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
71.text: "I'm glad you agree. But the wrongs of the past can still be undone by others."

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: He sighed and looked at me with narrowed eyes.

73.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
73.text: "I want to ask you to reconsider the targets of the emergency. It is still not too late."
73.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_YS"] == true) == false

74.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
74.text: "I'll be clear. You can still make it up to us. And I think you should take that opportunity."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: "The Young Sords orchestrated an attack at the Maroon Palace and murdered a member of the Assembly in cold blood. There is nothing to reconsider here."

77.speaker: Player
77.text: "Don't act like you have the upper hand, Mr. Kibener. You are the one who should make it up to me."

79.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
79.text: "No need for premature assumptions, Mr. President."

80.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
80.text: "Let's not imagine that scenario, Mr. President. Let me explain."

81.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
81.text: "Yes, yes. A justified purge. A classic campaign of anti-Sordist propaganda from the establishment. I get it."

82.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
82.text: "We know how it goes. Hire a mentally damaged individual to wreak societal havoc and blame a whole group of individuals for it."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "Isn't it ironic that you're the one who's saying this?"

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "You're the one putting undue blame on minorities. Particularly the Bludish community."

85.speaker: Player
85.text: "I'm sorry but I don't agree with that. The establishment is more aligned with your ideology than anything else."

86.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
86.text: "Are you saying I'm a hypocrite? Perhaps I am."

87.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
87.text: "Maybe it does seem that way from your perspective. Doesn't mean it's the truth."

88.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
88.text: "Nonetheless, none of that matters if you cannot hold onto your newly attained powers."

89.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
89.text: "Your emergency act may have you feeling invincible, but there are forces grander than you that are set on your destruction."

90.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
90.text: "I'll be straight with you. Your politics or intentions don't matter if you cannot hold onto your newly attained powers."

91.speaker: Petr Vectern
91.text: "You cannot speak that way to the president, Mr. Kibener. I hope -- for your sake -- that wasn't a threat."

92.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
92.text: "I'll be straight with you. Your politics or intentions don't matter if you cannot hold onto your newly attained powers."

93.speaker: Player
93.text: "Mr. Vice President is right. Be careful with your choice of words, Mr. Kibener."

94.speaker: Player
94.text: "It's okay, Petr. I want to know where he'll go with this."

95.speaker: Player
95.text: (Point at your armed security.) "I think you're forgetting that we're in an emergency. I advise you not to bite off any more than you can chew."

96.speaker: Narrator
96.text: I pointed at the heavily armed security forces that followed us from a distance. Kesaro took a long look at them and turned to us, smiling.

97.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
97.text: "Now, that was an actual threat. Wouldn't you agree, Mr. Vectern?"

99.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
99.text: "I actually wanted you to meet someone. We both have much to discuss with you. He'll be here any second now."

100.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
100.text: "What would be a more fitting act on such a day of unity than the establishment of mutual respect and cooperation?"

101.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
101.text: "I wish people would focus more on actions than words. But I will do my best."

102.speaker: Petr Vectern
102.text: "Well... Feel free to file a lawsuit, Mr. Kibener."

104.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
104.text: "As I said... The president is far from safe during this emergency. I am aware of the fissures forming between the administration and the Supreme Court. The Old Guard have you at their whim."

105.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
105.text: "I just wanted to confirm whether you are insistent on committing your own political suicide or not."

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "I'm not going to entertain you by taking part in your word games, Mr. Kibener."

107.speaker: Player
107.text: "You've heard wrong. There are no cracks between us."

108.speaker: Player
108.text: "Why would you care if it is a political suicide for me?"

109.speaker: Player
109.text: "The answer is: I am not. I am aware of the threat the Court poses but I won't be intimidated by it."

110.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
110.text: "I'm an honest man, so don't get me wrong. If it was only about you or the USP, I wouldn't care at all."

111.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
111.text: "But if the nationalist movement is getting the short end of the stick in this process, then we have a problem."

112.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
112.text: "Suit yourself, Mr. Rayne. But hear me out."

115.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
115.text: "Look. I never questioned your courage. Your logic, on the other hand..."

116.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
116.text: "Our suggestion is to finally enforce the official language of our country as stated in the constitution."

117.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
117.text: "We are working on the Unified Language Act. It is directly aimed at the breeding grounds of the Bludish Freedom Front."

118.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
118.text: "The bill will give the state a way to control the radicalization in these schools that teach Bludish nationalist propaganda. Without taking any rights away."

119.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
119.text: "I believe we already have the support of all the patriots within the Assembly."

121.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
121.text: "The police have infiltrated 32 BFF training grounds in remote towns around Bergia that posed as middle schools. Despite all the evidence, similar schools keep popping up."

122.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
122.text: "And so-called activists are constantly blocking Governor Bron's attempts to stop these schools, claiming he is attacking their *right to language*."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "Even if the Assembly supports it, I will surely be using my veto on it."

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "I'll sign the bill if it reaches me."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: "I'll have to read it in detail to decide if I can support it."

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: Suddenly, a man with a large build in a brown suit approached us. When we turned to greet him, I realized he was Remus Holstron. The Deputy of the National Front Party.

128.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
128.text: "If I were you, I wouldn't stand in the way of the majority, Mr. Rayne."

129.speaker: Petr Vectern
129.text: "So you want the support of the USP?"

130.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
130.text: "Your emergency is directly aimed at the proud nationalists of this country, Mr. Rayne. People are finally waking up to it."

131.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
131.text: "You had your own justification, of course. A classic campaign of anti-Sordist propaganda from the establishment. I get it."

132.speaker: Player
132.text: "Really, Mr. Kibener? When it's a Bludish person, it's Bludish terror, but when it's Sordish nationalists, it's a few mentally handicapped individuals?"

133.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
133.text: "You made an enemy out of Sordish nationalists -- people who have the deepest love for this nation."
133.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true  or Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true  or Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_TightenedImmigration"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Progressive"] == true  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_FinancialInvestment_UC"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Order_DecreasedInteriorFunding"] == true) == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Vetoed"] == true)

136.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
136.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_YS"] == true) == false

137.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
137.text: "Don't put words in my mouth, President Rayne."

138.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
138.text: "You cannot win a fight against the core values of Sords and Sordland. I hope you are aware of that mistake now."

139.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
139.text: "The Young Sords aren't some kind of a 'fringe group of militants' as your administration claims. You know whom they represent and how many stand behind them."

141.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
141.text: "What, are you bored already, Mr. Rayne?"

143.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
143.text: "You are making an enemy out of Sordish nationalists -- people who have the deepest love for this nation."
143.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true  or Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_TightenedImmigration"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Progressive"] == true  and  (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_FinancialInvestment_UC"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Order_DecreasedInteriorFunding"] == true) == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Vetoed"] == true) == false)

144.speaker: Player
144.text: "No. Please tell me about these *grander* forces. I want to hear it."

145.speaker: Petr Vectern
145.text: "And who might that be, Mr. Kibener?"

146.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
146.text: "My deputy, Remus Holstron. He wanted to personally congratulate you for your emergency policies."

152.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
152.text: "Especially after you isolated yourself and made everyone your enemy."

153.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
153.text: "What do you want me to say? You know your enemies better than me."

154.speaker: Player
154.text: "It's interesting to see you speak on behalf of an outlawed terror organization, Mr. Kibener. To be clear, are you admitting your ties to the Young Sords?"

155.speaker: Player
155.text: "If you really thought I'd be interested in such an offer, you're living in your dreams."

156.speaker: Player
156.text: "It's too late for that, Mr. Kibener. The Young Sords have overstepped and organized a political assassination in the heart of the capital. I cannot simply reverse my decision after that fact."

160.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
160.text: "I want you to reconsider your orders about the Young Sords. It's not too late to make amends. Besides, if there's an ally to be made, it is the nationalist youth."

161.speaker: Player
161.text: "What in the world is the *Iron Wall*?"

162.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
162.text: "You made an enemy of Sordland. I hope you are aware of that now."

163.speaker: Remus Holstron
163.text: "It's nice to finally meet you in person, Mr. President and Mr. Vice President."

164.speaker: Player
164.text: "It's great to see your party's wholehearted support. Thank you."

165.speaker: Petr Vectern
165.text: "The Iron Wall. The man behind... well, many things. Let's just say he's a bit of a legend within the nationalist movement."

167.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
167.text: "No need to thank us, Mr. Rayne."

168.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
168.text: "It's just an old nickname that stuck around. Nobody really calls him that anymore."

169.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
169.text: "While we wait, I wanted to quickly mention a few things that were occupying my mind recently."

171.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
171.text: "I am sure that it will pass and arrive on your desk, Mr. President. All I'm asking is for you not to veto it."

172.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
172.text: "Ah. There he is! Welcome, Mr. Holstron."

174.speaker: Player
174.text: "I'd also be happy to meet with him, Mr. Kibener."

175.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
175.text: "Thank you. There are a few things that have been occupying my mind recently."

180.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
180.text: "Fine. No comments. But at least hear this out."

181.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
181.text: "The Young Sords aren't some kind of a 'fringe group of militants' as your administration claimed. You know whom they represent and how many are behind them."

184.speaker: Narrator
184.text: We walked until we found a shady spot just outside the Jen Center of Culture.

185.speaker: Narrator
185.text: Kesaro leaned against the wall, pulled out a cigarette and lit it up with his Rippo lighter.

186.speaker: Player
186.text: "I always wanted to meet the Iron Wall himself. Today's my lucky day."

191.speaker: Player
191.text: "Have you forgotten common courtesy, Mr. Kibener? Are we not offering cigarettes to friends anymore?"

192.speaker: Player
192.text: "How long are we going to be waiting here exactly?"

193.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
193.text: "You bet, Mr. President. It's one of the first."

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: He passed a cigarette to me.

196.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
196.text: "Our flags fly above the clouds, Mr. Rayne. And from up there, our fallen brothers, our national pride, the Sordish spirit... They're all watching over us."

197.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
197.text: "And they surely watched in shame when the true patriots of this country were targeted with purely political reasons."

201.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
201.text: "The Bludish independence movement, for example... Not only do the separatists pose an existential risk to us, they also threaten our neighbors in Wehlen."

205.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
205.text: "I may not be fond of President Smolak, but our joint operation with the Wehzeks was certainly successful in stamping out the BFF. I consider that a great success."

207.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
207.text: "Don't worry. It won't take too long."

208.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
208.text: "Believe it or not, this lighter is the reason I'm alive today. I should be thankful that the damn assassin was a Blud. No wonder he was incompetent."

209.speaker: Narrator
209.text: I took a look at his lighter as he closed its lid. It was a regular Rippo, but its shape appeared to be malformed.

210.speaker: Narrator
210.text: Looking more closely, I could see a large circular dent in the chrome plating.

211.speaker: Narrator
211.text: He pulled on his collar to reveal a scar on his neck.

212.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
212.text: "Maybe I'll tell you the full story some other time. For now, I have some other things in mind."

213.speaker: Narrator
213.text: He took a drag from his cigarette and pointed at the giant flagpole in the plaza. I had to crane my neck to see the enormous Sordish flag flying from it.

214.speaker: Narrator
214.text: He gave me the lighter. It was obviously high-quality, but its shape appeared to be malformed.

221.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
221.text: "And they are surely ashamed of what we Sords are living through today. Ashamed of how the true patriots of this country are being targeted for purely political reasons."

222.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
222.text: "The lighter took the first shot. The second one grazed me right here."

226.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
226.text: "That brings me to the Religious Harmony Bill."

227.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
227.text: "Now, Rumburg will have a harder time trying to influence us from within. Let's not forget their caches of KA-74s in our country. You've done the right thing."

228.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
228.text: "That's right. They don't even know whom they are dealing with."

229.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
229.text: "Closing the borders with Wehlen has helped, but the countryside of Nargis and Bergia continues to be plagued by the BFF."

230.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
230.text: "Wehlen continues to be plagued by the BFF. They use their secret bases in the mountains to launch infiltrations into Sordland."

236.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
236.text: "They are a weaker nation both in heart and might. They won't have the capacity to handle the Bludish threat."

237.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
237.text: "Rumburg is using them to weaken us, and they might succeed if we do nothing to stop them. Let's not forget their caches of KA-74s in our country."

238.speaker: Player
238.text: "The support President Smolak received from United Contana was a concern, but realpolitik was the victor."

239.speaker: Player
239.text: "Rumburg and the BFF will both meet a bad end if they dare to divide Sordland."

240.speaker: Player
240.text: "We can't intervene in other countries. It would destabilize the region."

241.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
241.text: "A Sordish president has to do whatever is necessary to protect his people."

242.speaker: Player
242.text: "Wehlen could be a valuable ally in the future, now that we have established a closer relationship."

243.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
243.text: "Rumburg is using them to weaken us. Hopefully, our increased military funding will make sure their efforts won't bear fruit. But we need to stay vigilant. Let's not forget their caches of KA-74s in our country."

244.speaker: Player
244.text: "Wehlen can take care of their own problems, and we will take care of ours."

252.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
252.text: "Thanks to your support, the BFF and other extremist groups won't be able to use religion to organize and gain support among the common folk."

256.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
256.text: "But you decided to veto it. Why are you ignoring the problem? The Bludish are using Nurity as a tool in their quest for independence. This is a direct threat."

257.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
257.text: "If anything, we are not restrictive enough. But I will not dive into this further."

258.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
258.text: "In this case, doing nothing is far worse. The BFF is actively using priests in majority-Bludish areas. But let's not get off track."

259.speaker: Player
259.text: "The bill was practically a recruitment flyer for the BFF. The more of these we pass, the more followers they get."

260.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
260.text: "Thank you. I led the effort. I was happy but not surprised to receive so much support from my fellow MPs."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "It was too restrictive on the Bludish people. I couldn't let it pass."

262.speaker: Player
262.text: "The Bludish problem must be solved. We can't have an independence movement inside Sordland."

263.speaker: Player
263.text: "It was a well-written and strong bill. It would have been wrong to veto it."

264.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
264.text: "In an ideal world, yes. But as long as the BFF exists, that is not the world we live in."

265.speaker: Player
265.text: "We need to find a way where we can coexist without violence."

266.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
266.text: "I'm glad you and I agree on this issue."

267.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
267.text: "Our party and many members of parliament worked extremely hard on the proposal."

268.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
268.text: "Look. I don't mean to corner you on Victory Day like this, but I have to mention an important bill in the making."

269.speaker: Player
269.text: "Is your national pride so fragile that this will destroy it? I don't think so."

270.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
270.text: "You were fooled. They saw Sordland battling the recession and they pounced on it."

271.speaker: Player
271.text: "It was a necessary evil. Don't expect me to sit by while my people suffer."

272.speaker: Player
272.text: "Kesaro. I am the President. I won't allow you to talk to me like this."

274.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
274.text: "I fought for my country many times, and I have the scars to prove it. Can you say the same?"

275.speaker: Player
275.text: "I don't see anything wrong with accepting a helping hand."

277.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
277.text: "The NFP believes you sold our national pride for money."

278.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
278.text: "I won't waste my breath further on this matter, since you clearly don't understand."

282.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
282.text: "I also wanted to talk about the aid you received from United Contana."

283.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
283.text: "Do you think that's just free money? Do you think they offered it out of sheer goodwill?"

285.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
285.text: "I think it didn't last long enough to make a difference."

286.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
286.text: "Oh, you made more than one of those."

287.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
287.text: "The emergency was the right call but it didn't last long enough to make a difference."

290.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
290.text: "And they are surely concerned of the current circumstances the Sords have to go live through. One day you have an emergency, the next day the rules are different again."

291.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
291.text: "And they are surely applauding you for your determination in maintaining stability in this nation. Applauding how its true patriots are finally taking it back."

292.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
292.text: "Luckily that time is behind us now. Thankfully, you revoked that emergency before it was too late."

293.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
293.text: "Political uncertainty inside and exploitative pressures outside. It is an unusual time."

297.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
297.text: "Your fight against Bludish separatists and radical Malenyevists has been commendable, Mr. Rayne. I must thank you for it."

298.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
298.text: "You are making a grave mistake targeting the wrong people, Mr. Rayne."

299.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
299.text: "Albeit not enough by any means, your fight against the radical Malenyevists has been commendable, Mr. Rayne. I must thank you for it."
299.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == true)

300.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
300.text: "Albeit not enough by any means, your fight against Bludish separatists has been commendable, Mr. Rayne. I must thank you for it."
300.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_RY"] == true) == false)

301.speaker: Player
301.text: "Would you have thought the same if it wasn't your boys who were being targeted?"

302.speaker: Player
302.text: "It was a necessary decision to make. For the time."

303.speaker: Player
303.text: "Mistakes were made but the past is in the past."

305.speaker: Player
305.text: "Am I supposed to be impressed with the theatrics?"

307.speaker: Player
307.text: "Am I supposed to be impressed with the theatrics?"

308.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
308.text: "What? You expected me to come up with a witty response claiming I would?"

310.speaker: Player
310.text: "Were you not supportive of the emergency?"

311.speaker: Player
311.text: "Mistakes were made but the past is in the past."

312.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
312.text: "It's true. And I respect you for admitting that."

313.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
313.text: "It was hardly a *necessary* decision, Mr. President. You know that."

315.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
315.text: "Does that mean you completely trust the Old Guard and will not budge on your position?"

316.speaker: Player
316.text: "Why don't you answer my question first?"

317.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
317.text: "Well, are you telling me that you completely trust the Old Guard and will not budge on your position?"

318.speaker: Narrator
318.text: Petr looked at me in surprise.

319.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
319.text: "Don't you have the power to fabricate an answer to that question yourself and do whatever you wish with it? I refuse to play that game."

320.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
320.text: "You answer me. Do you or don't you trust the Old Guard? And is your position flexible?"

321.speaker: Player
321.text: "I didn't say anything about trusting the Old Guard."

322.speaker: Player
322.text: "I don't trust the Old Guard the same way I don't trust you."

324.speaker: Player
324.text: "You know what? Let's hear what you're exactly offering here."

325.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
325.text: "The Old Guard will not let you free from their hook. You know they can strike back at you at any time."

326.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
326.text: "If the nationalists supported you, the emergency would have been much more effective against its 'true' targets. And you wouldn't need to fear Hawker as much."

328.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
328.text: "The Old Guard will not let you free from their hook. You know that they can strike back at you at any time."

329.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
329.text: "It is a shame to see you make enemies of everybody. But if you're willing to continue on this path, I'll gladly watch your demise."

330.speaker: Player
330.text: "Enough with your threats. If you're delaying the celebrations for this talk, I'll take my leave."

331.speaker: Player
331.text: "You are making an enemy of Sordland at this very moment, Mr. Kibener. I advise you to back off before it's too late."

332.speaker: Player
332.text: "It's too late to complain, Mr. Kibener. The Young Sords have overstepped and organized a political assassination in the heart of the capital. I cannot simply reverse my decision after that fact."

333.speaker: Player
333.text: "It's interesting to see you speak on behalf of an outlawed terror organization, Mr. Kibener. To be clear, are you admitting your ties to the Young Sords?"

334.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
334.text: "I'm not delaying anything. If you're willing to abandon Sordland's largest Victory Day celebrations, feel free to do so."

336.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
336.text: "Don't you have the power to fabricate an answer to that question yourself and do whatever you wish with it? I refuse to play that game."

337.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
337.text: "I may back off but others may not."

341.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
341.text: "You are a traitor to the cause."

343.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
343.text: "You know what I'm trying to say... But are you willing to have that conversation?"

344.speaker: Player
344.text: "You know what? I am willing to hear you out. I will consider a reversal on the ban of the Young Sords -- if you can *convince* me."

352.speaker: Remus Holstron
352.text: "I must say I am very supportive of the emergency, Mr. Rayne."

356.speaker: Remus Holstron
356.text: "The Sordists and the wider Sordish nationalist movement hold the consensus view that the act was justified."

357.speaker: Remus Holstron
357.text: "I must say you are very lucky to survive the journey to central Jen, Mr. Rayne. This city is the stronghold of the Sordists."

358.speaker: Remus Holstron
358.text: "It is good to see you both in Jen today. This means a lot to us."

359.speaker: Remus Holstron
359.text: "The Sordists and the wider Sordish nationalist movement hold the consensus view that this emergency is targeting them as a whole."

364.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
364.text: "I've already talked to Mr. President about a possible reversal of the wrongs that have been made."

365.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
365.text: "He is willing to compromise for our support."

367.speaker: Remus Holstron
367.text: "The event is about to begin. Why don't we slowly walk over to the plaza?"

370.speaker: Player
370.text: "I don't care what the nationalists think."

371.speaker: Player
371.text: "Are you threatening the President of Sordland?"

372.speaker: Player
372.text: "No more threats! Both of you will face consequences for your actions today."

374.speaker: Player
374.text: "Look at the time. Is the event starting already?"

378.speaker: Petr Vectern
378.text: "Enough of this, you three. Let's go to the damn plaza and get this event over with already."

381.speaker: Narrator
381.text: He looked at me straight in the eye.

382.speaker: Remus Holstron
382.text: "Mr. Rayne. The nationalists are willing to give you their support if you are willing to protect them."

383.speaker: Remus Holstron
383.text: "And if you reverse the ban on the Young Sords, and give your support to the group, you will be in a much stronger position enforcing your emergency powers."

384.speaker: Remus Holstron
384.text: "If you're willing to do that, and help us with a few requests, we can have this conversation in detail. I can answer any questions you have."

385.speaker: Player
385.text: "On a second thought, I don't want to involve myself with the Young Sords. We are not having this conversation."

386.speaker: Player
386.text: "On a second thought, I think I should report you both for supporting terrorism."

387.speaker: Remus Holstron
387.text: "Go ahead, Mr. Rayne. We have done nothing wrong and the police knows this."

388.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
388.text: "It's actually about to begin. Follow me."

389.speaker: Remus Holstron
389.text: "Go ahead, Mr. Rayne. Remain a puppet of the Sollists."

390.speaker: Remus Holstron
390.text: "Good luck with your masters in the Old Guard."

391.speaker: Petr Vectern
391.text: "It's a celebration, remember? Let's go to the damn plaza and get this event over with."

394.speaker: Player
394.text: "I'm willing to consider it but I need to know about these additional requests and exactly what you are offering."

395.speaker: Remus Holstron
395.text: "In return for giving you full support, the nationalists would expect you to show them that you are a true patriot."

397.speaker: Narrator
397.text: He looked me straight in the eye.

398.speaker: Remus Holstron
398.text: "President Rayne. The nationalists are willing to give you their support if you are willing to protect them."

399.speaker: Remus Holstron
399.text: "I'm referring particularly to the Young Sords. Many in the organization feel the urge to support you directly in your efforts against our enemies."

400.speaker: Remus Holstron
400.text: "If you're willing to cooperate with the Young Sords, we can have this conversation in detail. I can answer any questions you have about a possible alliance."

401.speaker: Player
401.text: "I thought you only wanted to unban the Young Sords. What are these requests?"

402.speaker: Remus Holstron
402.text: "However, revoking the ban alone won't be enough to erase the trauma you brought upon them."

403.speaker: Remus Holstron
403.text: "And finally, we want you to sign the Unified Education Act when it reaches you. We already have the support of the Assembly and it would be a step in the right direction if you do not use your veto powers on it."
403.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Progressive"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_TightenedImmigration"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_SnO_Investigate_Opposition"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_Removed"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] > 0) and ((Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] > 0) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Order_IncreasedInteriorFunding"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Military_IncreasedFunding"] == false) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_YS"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Turn05_SnO_Investigate_Opposition"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_TightenedImmigration"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.Turn04_PSnW_Education_Progressive"] == true)

407.speaker: Remus Holstron
407.text: "What do you want to know about first?"

408.speaker: Player
408.text: "First, tell me what the Young Sords can offer me."

409.speaker: Player
409.text: "First, I want to hear your demands."

410.speaker: Remus Holstron
410.text: "First and foremost, you will revoke the ban on the Young Sords and recognize them as a legal organization."

414.speaker: Remus Holstron
414.text: "With the Young Sords on your side, you will be in a much stronger position to enforce your emergency powers."

415.speaker: Remus Holstron
415.text: "And judging by the current relationship you have with the Supreme Court, it would be a good idea for you to have strong allies outside of their direct reach."

416.speaker: Player
416.text: "Very intriguing. I'm willing to discuss the possibilities."

417.speaker: Player
417.text: "Let's talk about how we can help each other."

418.speaker: Player
418.text: "I'm sorry, but I don't want to involve myself with the Young Sords."

421.speaker: Petr Vectern
421.text: "You know I don't necessarily enjoy the emergency. But at this point, why not hear the Iron Wall out?"

422.speaker: Petr Vectern
422.text: "As much as I hate to involve ourselves with the Young Sords, he has a point about the Court. You need strong allies against them."

423.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
423.text: "The Old Guard will not let you free from their hook. You know they can strike back at you at any time. We can help each other out."

424.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
424.text: "If the nationalists supported you, the emergency would be much more effective against its targets. And you wouldn't need to fear Hawker as much."

425.speaker: Petr Vectern
425.text: "'Effective' in what way exactly, Mr. Kibener?"

426.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
426.text: "You know what I'm trying to say... But are you willing to have that conversation?"

427.speaker: Player
427.text: "You know what? Having the Young Sords support me is not a bad idea. Let's talk."

430.speaker: Remus Holstron
430.text: "The Young Sords can give you on-the-ground support that the state institutions cannot provide. A helping hand to steer the country towards your cause."

431.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
431.text: "Well... I guess we can start walking towards the plaza. The event is about to start."

436.speaker: Remus Holstron
436.text: "You should already have an idea of what they're capable of. With protection from the President himself, they will surely have the power to eliminate any obstacle that stands in your way."

437.speaker: Player
437.text: "Quit beating around the bush, Mr. Holstron. You are offering me an extrajudicial solution to political problems. Isn't that right?"

438.speaker: Player
438.text: "Can you give me more concrete examples?"

439.speaker: Player
439.text: "But how do I know they won't turn against me one day?"

440.speaker: Player
440.text: "I like the idea already, Mr. Holstron."

441.speaker: Remus Holstron
441.text: "You don't. Neither do I. Who truly knows what the future will bring?"

442.speaker: Remus Holstron
442.text: "Trust is mutual, Mr. Rayne. As long as both sides understand each other, there would be no reason to end a beneficial cooperation."

444.speaker: Remus Holstron
444.text: "No, I cannot. But I can tell you whether what's on your mind can be done or not."

446.speaker: Remus Holstron
446.text: "But I'm not responsible for anything the Young Sords might or might not want to offer you."

449.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
449.text: "The support of a such a massive non-governmental organization would surely be useful to you, Mr. Rayne."

450.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
450.text: "Ask away and we'll try our best to answer."

451.speaker: Player
451.text: "How can the Young Sords help us enforce the emergency?"

452.speaker: Player
452.text: "I know the Young Sords are well-connected with the NFP. How can they support me if they're aligned with our rivals?"

453.speaker: Player
453.text: "What if there are problematic individuals who require... being handled?"

454.speaker: Player
454.text: "The Court is a problem. What can we do to protect the emergency and the administration?"

455.speaker: Remus Holstron
455.text: "The enemies of the state are the enemies of the Young Sords, Mr. Rayne."

456.speaker: Remus Holstron
456.text: "Ms. Graf's security forces are doing a good job enforcing the rules on the ground, but they might still have some gaps that need filling in."

460.speaker: Remus Holstron
460.text: "They can help the security forces on the ground where necessary. I'm sure that would be very valuable, considering the current lack of funding for the police."

461.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
461.text: "An alliance with the Young Sords means an unofficial alliance with the nationalist movement, Mr. Rayne."

462.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
462.text: "As long as our policies stay aligned, we are no rivals. Nationalists being in charge of this nation has only benefits for both of us."

463.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
463.text: "Hell, maybe it's even about time for the USP to form an official alliance with the NFP. We'd be stronger together."

464.speaker: Remus Holstron
464.text: "If it's the elections you're worried about, don't. If you sustain the emergency until that point, let's just say we'd be happy to support your campaign."

465.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
465.text: "I've heard rumors that you already have the means to handle that."

469.speaker: Remus Holstron
469.text: "If your definition of 'problematic' aligns with ours, I don't think it would be difficult to arrange something."

470.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
470.text: "But of course, even you probably don't have absolute control over those forces. If they prove to be unreliable, the nationalist youth would be happy to help."

472.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
472.text: "The Court itself isn't the main problem. It's certain individuals who hold the power to impeach you whenever necessary."

473.speaker: Remus Holstron
473.text: "And their adulterated Sollist philosophy, of course... This illusion of *unity* they fabricated has long poisoned our nation. It is time the true Sords take the power back."

474.speaker: Remus Holstron
474.text: "I believe the Sordists are done cooperating with them. If you prove to be the strong leader you're portraying yourself as, they'd be happy to plan a move against the Court."

487.speaker: Remus Holstron
487.text: "They'll need resources to be able to rebuild again. You'll need to arrange a 'transfer' of finances."

488.speaker: Remus Holstron
488.text: "We are also aware of the investigations being conducted on both opposition parties. You will immediately stop the investigations into the NFP."

489.speaker: Remus Holstron
489.text: "You will write a decree to tighten immigration. Effective immediately."

490.speaker: Remus Holstron
490.text: "And you will order the complete halt of your education reforms. There is no possible way we can accept the removal of nationalist doctrines from our curriculums."

491.speaker: Remus Holstron
491.text: "Finally, you will reinstate the Energy Protection Act as it was enacted by Tarquin Soll. We have to reverse this exploitative scheme immediately."

492.speaker: Remus Holstron
492.text: "If you can do that, you will have the nationalist movement and the Young Sords behind you."

493.speaker: Remus Holstron
493.text: "Finally, you will make use of the remaining government budget and transfer emergency funds to the Ministry of Interior to strengthen the emergency."

585.text: "Now why don't we head back towards the plaza? The event is about to start."

587.speaker: Remus Holstron
587.text: "Anyway, our presence is expected at the plaza. Shall we make our way over?"

591.speaker: Remus Holstron
591.text: "Good to see you again after a long time, Mr. President and Mr. Vice President."
